entry.title: My Deaf Mom
entry.summary: She lived her life with an immature desire. Dancing and singing, her…
entry.content:
She lived her life with an immature desire.
Dancing and singing, her face lit a room.
But like a firecracker before the boom,
many often held their breath while by her.
 
I remember once, while near that line of fire,
I blushed, a boy of five, from her strong fume.
Her lips spewing forth in an obscene plume,
while she alone would not hear the deafening ire.
 
Then I’d relay the circumspect reply,
from a confused face speaking through her child,
as my mother lit a fresh cigarette.
 
Rewinding the tape with her careful eye,
she watched me imitate the words which riled,
never showing me a small sign of regret.

entry.title: Bread
entry.summary: I smell the bread baking and I’m reminded of your soft hands…
entry.content:
I smell the bread baking
and I’m reminded of your soft hands
touching that fleshy dough.
You make me hungry.
 
As steam and hot scent
escape from the oven door,
I see our reflection in the glass.
My face is covered in sweat.
 
Though you give me a generous slice,
hot and sweet with salted butter;
even while the taste still lingers,
I want more.

entry.title: Autumn
entry.summary: I looked out for you, but frost covered my window. Summer, did…
entry.content:
I looked out for you,
but frost covered my window.
Summer, did you leave?

entry.summary: Lipstick red, your massive hips bulge above supple feet, as my finger…
entry.content:
Lipstick red,
your massive hips
bulge above supple feet,
as my finger gently traces
their obscene curve.
Anticipating that
provocative,
pulsing,
power,
perched
between your thick thighs,
I take my seat
and
I turn the key.

entry.title: Liquor
entry.summary: The poetic word is potent. Like one hundred and seven proof bourbon,…
entry.content:
The poetic word is potent.
Like one hundred and seven proof
bourbon,
it makes me drunk.

Plenty of pages of prose
are distilled in
a single
stanza.

It is irresistible as
I swirl it in my mouth.
Sniff it.
Taste it.

Breathe it in.

I hold it up to the light
to peer into its soul.
and with voracious appetite,
I invert its glass until

the

last

drip

slides
slowly
south

onto my 
silver
tongue.

entry.title: Paper Airplane
entry.summary: If you chance find this poem, please do not attempt reply. Just…
entry.content:
If you chance find this poem,
please do not attempt reply.
Just fold it back into its shape
and toss it toward the sky.
 
I launched it late last night,
out the window in my room,
a sort of self-made prison space
above my future tomb.
 
Thirty years I’ve toiled
on this edifice of gold.
Performing tasks I scarce enjoy,
a slab of me I sold.
 
Just a wishful poet,
when you cut me to my core.
Perhaps, some day, I’ll muster strength
and become someone more.
 
This airplane sent aloft,
out on the chill night air,
it is a verse from Morpheus,
a hope, a dream, my prayer.

entry.title: Rowing
entry.summary: The oars cut thin, they split the calm, cold lake. My legs,…
entry.content:
The oars cut thin, they split the calm, cold lake.
My legs, still stiff, propel me back, but slow.
My back and arms repeat that work they know.
Now pace makes fast and hard, I’m wide awake.
 
Each stroke proceeds to build consuming ache.
Each drop of sweat, its wish, a breeze would blow.
Each pull, protests my next command to row.
I lift a hand to drink, in hope my thirst to slake.
 
This pause so short revives my mind and soul.
I look and see the beauty of this place.
The fog about, it lays like a smoky rug.
 
A gar I glimpse, as it swims inside a shoal.
Now wind I feel, move quick across my face,
And God leans down blessing me with His hug.

entry.title: Jewelry
entry.summary: In the springtime of our life you brought forth a bud which…
entry.content:
In the springtime of our life
you brought forth a bud
which so very slowly grew.
 
Your peridot leaves shone
nourishing this delicate gem
so pregnant with promise.
 
With exhausting care and
tears and prayer you coaxed
forth a golden citrine flower.
 
A single maternal blossom
nurtured as a simple act of love
fulfilled in six complex petals.
 
And these many years, my great joy
has been to gaze upon this lily
and into the eyes of its able gardener.

entry.title: Six Feet
entry.summary: We woke and gazed out, seeing a violent stream now coursed, rapidly…
entry.content:
We woke and gazed out,
seeing a violent stream now coursed,
rapidly between us and our neighbor's place.
 
A strid, deadly if crossed,
like that of which Wordsworth wrote,
recalling the force of prayer.
 
Strid from the Old English,
word "Stryth" meaning "turmoil",
recalling the force of water.
 
Strid for the deceptive possibility,
of easily striding across so narrow a gap,
recalling the force of hope.
 
Just six feet wide,
was Wordsworth's ancient strid,
in its ancient course past Bolton priory.
 
Just six feet wide,
but taking into its icy depths so many,
lads and ladies and lovers who dared to pass.
 
Just six feet of social distance,
but no less a thief of friendship,
than the six feet of an earthy grave.
 
"Strangled by a merciless force",
the priory cut off from the body,
leaving St. Mary and St. Cuthbert alone in prayer.
 
But Moses’ staff was lifted high,
and God parted the sea enough,
to consume the six foot width of Pharoah's chariot.
 
And God kept faith,
Delivering His people out of bondage,
by deftly closing that six foot gap.
 
And His Son kept faith,
Delivering His people out of bondage,
by sacrificially closing the six foot depth of the grave.

entry.title: A Week of Quarantine
entry.summary: I: I searched an hour for my pjs so that I could…
entry.content:
I:
 
I searched an hour for my pjs
so that I could go to bed .
Quarantine has blurred my days
and wreaked havoc with my head.
A quick glance in the mirror,
I see my sanity foregone.
The pajama search abruptly ended.
I already have them on.
 
II:
 
My office space keeps moving
as I go from call to call.
Piano practice sends me upstairs
behind our bedroom wall.
Then in comes mom with Ana
to put her down for nap.
So I descend the stairs again.
End this quarantine ASAP!
 
III:
 
I’m rowing down the Schuylkill
in a race against a crew.
The art museum is up ahead
and the Rocky statue too.
Now I run across a mountainscape
and through an Alpine town.
Such fantasies! They fill my head.
I hate exercise in lockdown.
 
IV:
 
Go out to eat and see a show
the Governor just said.
It’s back to normal and back to school
so get out of your bed.
Stay in your house or six feet apart
is no longer the rule.
I dream of this most every day.
Oh! Today is April Fool.
 
V:
 
Office life is underrated
with meetings face to face.
You can criticize a job done poor
and put them in their place.
But in quarantine while on the phone
you dare not scream and yell.
The boss, she’ll hear you acting up.
She’ll come and ring your bell.
 
VI:
 
“Thank God it’s Friday,”
has lost all of the appeal.
For tomorrow will be like today
without a different feel.
I wonder did we lose,
the weekend or the week?
Is boredom about to go away?
Or is it even close to peak?
 
VII:
 
Log scale graphs are useful
for showing change in rate.
In visualizing the second derivative
they really work out great.
But if you want real people
to understand your math.
Please use less than/greater.
When you project contagion path.
